source.note: Mirror of the venture manifest + the business-plans inventory. The Worker cannot fetch the venture repo at runtime: it is private, and the Worker holds no GitHub token — so this mirror is the live source for GET /v11/ventures. Refresh by PR whenever the venture manifest changes (the Phase 1 manifest PR updates this file). The source SHA above is how staleness is checked: if the venture repo's manifest.yaml SHA differs, this mirror is stale.

ventures.real_purpose: The "Sovereign Imagination Engine": takes a person's idea, extracted through questions and reality-checked before a dollar moves, and orchestrates a verified human workforce plus an AI agent swarm to make it real. Full doctrine already written (soul, constitution, architecture, legal-reality, an evidence ledger tagging every claim Verified/Unverified/Rejected).
ventures.notes: Closest match in this whole manifest for how `venture` itself should be structured — CLAUDE.md boot sequence, docs/ doctrine set, .claude/agents + .claude/skills. Built from a founding hand-off that was dissected by its own harshest critic before becoming doctrine.

ventures.real_purpose: A household device consolidating washer/dryer, crypto mining (Proof-of- Cleanliness), distributed AI compute, and personal banking into one unit. Massive vision library (10 volumes: vision, architecture, contracts, business model, partnerships, implementation, perspectives, monopoly thesis, philanthropy, legacy) — pure doctrine/pitch, zero code.
ventures.notes: Largest pure-vision repo of the seven. No `.claude/agents` or `.claude/skills` — a self-contained fact-sheet CLAUDE.md instead of a boot-sequence one, unlike SVFG.

ventures.real_purpose: An AI "Governance Compiler": turns plain-language organizational intent into deployable governance rules (JSON-LD/YAML/Python/JS/Solidity/ Markdown), deployable to Discord/Slack/Notion/blockchain. Full backend architecture documented (Node/Express + Python/FastAPI, Postgres, Redis, Temporal, LangChain) — README reads production-ready.
ventures.notes: Only the README was read this pass — unlike herDao, the actual source tree under this claimed architecture has not yet been checked file-by-file against what main.py-equivalent entrypoints actually import. Needs the same deep-dive herDao got before trusting "production-ready" at face value.

ventures.real_purpose: A gamified life-simulation app connecting digital decisions to real-world outcomes (financial literacy, entrepreneurship, community, personal growth) taught through a game. Rust/Dioxus/WASM.
ventures.notes: Level 0 ("The Gate") is real, implemented, tested, and verified end-to-end per the repo's own README — the one venture in this manifest that already has genuinely running, verified code, not just a spec. Levels 1-5 documented, not built. Has the terser IRL-style CONSTITUTION.md (5 numbered non-negotiable laws) this manifest's own docs/CONSTITUTION.md is modeled on.

ventures.real_purpose: A decentralized trucking-logistics OS: AI load-to-driver dispatch matching (LightGBM), real-time Geotab telematics ingestion, deactivation due-process enforcement, WARN Act compliance across federal + state law, an SBA loan eligibility engine, and an ERC-721 TruckNFT with a 45/45/10 equity split.
ventures.notes: Repo name (herDao) does not match its real content (Dispatcher DAO) — noted, not silently corrected. Deep-dived 2026-08-18: main.py imports api.routers.{auth,drivers,loads,compliance,telematics,wellness,payments, nft_tokens,disputes} — 9 of 14 documented routers have no file anywhere in the repo, and the 5 that do exist sit flat at repo root instead of inside the api/routers/, auth/, ml/models/ package paths their own imports require, so nothing here boots as committed. Verdict: rebuild the shape, keep the content — the logic (LightGBM weights, WARN Act state tables, SBA NAICS risk data, the equity-split contract) is real and detailed. DispaFrontend's src/App.jsx is a self-contained investor-pitch demo with hardcoded sample data and zero real API calls — a sales asset, not a working client for herDao's API. Full findings: ventures/dispatcher-dao/NOTES.md.

ventures.real_purpose: TheCopy is the real, actively-developed lead-generation and outreach Command Center (v1.3.1 as of 2026-08-14 — the most recently touched of all seven ventures): a LangGraph agent with lead-auditor/outreach-writer/ copywriter/process-lead sub-agents, a GitHub Pages public lead-capture form, a Command Center console. pipeline369-scraper is a free, self-hosted Google Maps lead scraper — its own README says it's the first real implementation of TheCopy's Pipeline/PIPELINE.md "Phase 1" targeting spec (reviews_count < 10, avg_rating >= 3.5, website != null), built because that spec only ever described a paid Apify actor.
ventures.notes: A real cross-venture dependency confirmed from the scraper's own README, not guessed — this is the clearest "two repos, one venture" case of the seven.

ventures.real_purpose: Was empty at first clone (2026-08-18) — no commits, no branch. This scaffold (manifest.yaml, CLAUDE.md, docs/, ventures/) is its genesis commit. Its own real purpose, if any beyond being the Ventures-program map, is not yet defined — ask the founder before assuming one.
ventures.notes: This is the meta/index repo itself — the map of the other six, plus the home of the capability-gap protocol and (once built) the sandbox-run record. Not a business venture in the same sense as the other six.

plans_note: 23 business plans in TehutiRaEl/venture under plans/ (from the 2026-11-11 Drive placement; inventory: VENTURE_PLANS_INVENTORY.md). Four relate to ventures already in this manifest (dispatcher-dao, v2d, svfg, the-aetherial-crucible). The full plan texts stay in the private venture repo and are NOT served by this endpoint — only this inventory. Word counts are from the placement inventory. HONEST FLAG: the per-plan counts in that inventory sum to 321,455 words, but the inventory's own stated total is 320,135 — a 1,320-word discrepancy inside the source inventory, not resolved here. plans_total_words above is the computed sum of the listed per-plan counts.
